chunks.arabic_text: عُرُيُونُ الْأَخْبَارِ: الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمَ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَنْ أَبِي الْجَارُودِ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، عَنْ جَابِرَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْأَنْصَارِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Uyun al-Akhbar: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far, from Jabir ibn Abdallah al-Ansari who said:

chunks.arabic_text: دَخَلْتُ عَلَى فَاطِمَ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ وَبَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا لَوْحٌ فِيهِ أَسْمَاءُ الْأَوْصِيَاءِ فَعَدَدْتُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ آخِرَهُمُ الْقَائِمُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنْهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ وَأَرْبَعَةٌ مِنْهُمْ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: I entered to meet Fatima (peace be upon her) and found a tablet in front of her containing the names of the Awsiya (Heirs). I counted twelve, the last of them being the Qaim (peace be upon him). Three of them were named Muhammad and four of them were named Ali (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This hadith from *Ayn al-Akhbar* highlights the concept of *Ismah* (infallibility) and divine designation (*Nass*) by presenting Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) as a custodian of a tablet listing the twelve Imams. The specific enumeration of three Muhammads and four Alis underscores the continuity of prophetic lineage, while identifying the Qaim as the final Imam reinforces the Shia belief in the occultation and eventual return of al-Mahdi. This narration serves as a key textual evidence for the number and names of the Imams in Shia theology.
en.seo_question: What did the tablet in front of Fatima (peace be upon her) contain regarding the Imams?

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The Heirs or Successors, referring to the Imams
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Qaim, referring to the twelfth Imam, al-Mahdi
key_terms.فَاطِمَ: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon her)
